# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 1 (Bi-Vb Np1)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Np1
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 1
**Title (English, from literature):** The training rule on collecting almsbowls
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-np1
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul6.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pattasannicaya* ("The training rule on collecting almsbowls") is the opening rule of the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* (relinquishment with confession) section in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates the possession of almsbowls among nuns, providing that a nun who keeps or accumulates more than one bowl must relinquish the surplus bowl and confess the transgression [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels for this rule exist in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (*Np* 1) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (*Np* 1), as well as across the monastic codes of other early Buddhist schools [SuttaCentral]. Corresponding rules on bowl accumulation are preserved in the Chinese versions of the Dharmaguptaka (*Np* 24), Mahīśāsaka (*Np* 30), Sarvāstivāda (*Np* 19), Mūlasarvāstivāda (*Np* 20), and Mahāsāṅghika (*Np* 14) traditions, in the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga* (*Np* 14), and in the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition (*Np* 20) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus confirms cross-language alignment between this Pali rule and the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), as well as matches with the Tibetan *Ekottarakarmaśataka* (D4118) and *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the rule shares substantial formulaic text reuse with parallel bowl and robe legislation in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*—most prominently *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 21 (over 9,800 characters) and *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 1—as well as various Vinaya Khandhaka chapters (including the *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka*, *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka*, and *Samuccayakkhandhaka*) and post-canonical commentaries and manuals such as the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
